'''Jwalshik Wilford''' (born September 3, 1968)  is a Nigerian chemist. Before his appointment on 1 June 2018, he was a deputy director of the [[Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria|Federal Capital Territory]] Water Board where he served most of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/wilford-jwalshik-47952b87/|title=LinkedIn|last=|first=|date=September 5, 2019|website=LinkedIn|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=September 5, 2019}}</ref> He is a fellow of the Institute of Chartered Chemists of Nigeria and the Chemical Society of Nigeria. His research interests are in the areas of water safety, contaminants of emerging concerns in raw water sources and the distribution network and new methods of water analyses and treatment.

== Career ==

On 1 June 2018, Wilford was appointed as the Registrar/CEO of Institute of Chartered Chemists of Nigeria (ICCON),<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vanguardngr.com/2018/06/fg-appoints-new-registrar-iccon/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=FG appoints new Registrar for ICCON|date=2018-06-20|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.von.gov.ng/chartered-chemists-of-nigeria-to-establish-research-centre/|title=Chartered Chemists of Nigeria to establish research centre|last=Nasir|first=Lantana|date=2019-07-25|newspaper=[[Voice of Nigeria]]|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> succeeding Mrs Kujore M. Fowotade as the third substantive Registrar/CEO of the institute.

He is a member of the Scientific Advisory Board, [[Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons|Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.opcw.org/about-us/subsidiary-bodies/scientific-advisory-board|title=Scientific Advisory Board|website=OPCW|language=en|access-date=2019-08-30}}</ref>
